q: I feel like I’m reading many different things about newborn sleep and feeling like a failure.
cx: Mother of a 6-week-old sleeping 2–3-hour stretches; she and her husband do shifts.

q: I already feel stressed about “ruining” her sleep and setting her up for bad habits - needing to nurse in order to fall sleep, accidentally waking her up when she’s crying but is still technically asleep, I don’t know. I’m just worried about everything and what I’m doing wrong.
cx: What she fears she is getting wrong at six weeks.

q: I’m not expecting it to be soon, I’m just feeling a bit lonely and behind.
cx: Reply to a parent describing when longer stretches started for them.

q: For the first time in ages I’m traveling alone with baby and my family , and I have caved into the pressure of not returning to the hotel for a proper bedtime for two days in a row .
cx: First-time mother who travels for work and always plans around her 1-year-old's naps.

q: THE GUILT IS KILLING ME , i feel like I’m making my baby suffer for no real reason other than family pressure .
cx: After two late nights back at the hotel at 10pm.

q: Last night was a breaking point for me he had a bottle at 7:30 to go to bed that was 8 ounces he woke up at 10 o’clock drink another 8 ounces, woke up at midnight drink another 8 ounces demanded more Bubba had four more ounces puked because he drank way too much milk and cried for another bottle and was up until 2 AM
cx: Parent of an 18-month-old who only falls asleep with a bottle after the dummy was stopped at 14 months.

q: So if anyone could give me some serious advice (like should I give him a sippy tonight with milk or just no milk at all) or a pep talk on how I’m supposed to get through this cold turkey and how beautiful it is on the other side.
cx: Wants both concrete steps and encouragement.

q: When we stopped the binky it was ROUGH a full week of crying and screaming for it but accepting the bottle as a full replacement eventually.
cx: The dummy came off cold turkey at 14 months; the bottle took its place.

q: I asked for no judgement and I’m feeling very judged. I’m not asking about brushing I’m asking about tips to getting rid of a bottle and help on how to get him to sleep. Reddit can be so helpful sometimes and also so not at the same time
cx: Replies focused on the child's teeth instead of sleep, in two subs.

q: My second daughter is three weeks old and she is a tough baby so far compared to my first.
cx: Stay-at-home parent of a 3-week-old and a 3-year-old.

q: I have a toddler at home who is three and honestly, I just feel physically and mentally exhausted by the end of the day.
cx: The newborn will not be put down at all by day.

q: I’m not expecting every nap to be in a bassinet or in a crib especially this young, but it would be nice to at least get a half hour during the day where I don’t have to be holding her in some type of way.
cx: Her modest goal.

q: Felt like these were very solid signs of being able to start a bit earlier than the standard 4mo. But we are fully prepared to just wait if tonight is a disaster. But wanted to attempt it.
cx: Parent starting Ferber on a 14-week-old after two weeks of Huckleberry logs.

q: We love her to the moon and back, and I dread every morning when I have to walk out the door.
cx: Parent writing about his girlfriend ('Mom') and their 8-week-old who will not sleep independently.

q: We have tried scheduled feedings and naps, playtime and tummy time, different swaddles, sleeping in the bassinet, warming the bassinet before putting her down, sleep shifts between Mom and me
cx: The list of what they tried.

q: Mom and I finally caved and got her a pacifier after doing a lot of research over the past week, but I’m afraid it won’t be the solution either. Her pediatrician told us this is normal and that it should get better eventually…  that was at her two week checkup.
cx: What the paediatrician said, six weeks earlier.

q: Mom is also worried about finances and returning to part-time work in two weeks. Are we in the best financial position? No. But I’m making it work the best I can.
cx: Money and work on top of the nights.

q: I’m posting this without telling mom, I fear if I info dump all this she’ll feel even more overwhelmed and stressed. I love my daughter. But I am are tired. We are tired, overwhelmed, and scared that we’re doing something wrong.
cx: The father's own state.

q: I always see memes and tiktok videos about bedtime being a marathon or a fight and thought thank goodness I don’t have that issue.
cx: Parent of a nearly-3-year-old content in her cot, weighing a move to a twin bed.

q: before he got sick he was sleeping pretty well. Going to bed on his own and waking just once overnight to eat. I sleep trained using CIO at 6 months. Now he will not go down on his own and wakes multiple times a night and will not go down without nursing
cx: Mother of an 8-month-old ill for weeks; training has unravelled.

q: I tried CIO on a whim a couple nights ago and he cried for over an hour before I just gave up & nursed him. He’s still sick. He’s been sick for so long. What are my options? I can’t keep going on this little sleep.
cx: A retrain attempt while the baby is still unwell.

q: Literally the day he turned 3 months old it was like he forgot that sleep was a thing? He only wants to sleep if I’m holding him, his bassinet is his mortal enemy and I have tried EVERYTHING.
cx: Exclusively breastfeeding mother; good 3–5-hour stretches ended at three months.

q: the second his body hits that bassinet it’s like he’s chugged 45 energy drinks. I am alone at nights and have barely been getting 4 hours of sleep for way too long and I need more sleep, I’m literally on my last straw.
cx: Nights are hers alone.

q: I can’t believe I’m saying this but I wish he was a little potato newborn again.
cx: Asking whether this is the 4-month regression and how long it lasts.

q: I tried while he was in his bassinet and after 3.5 hours of 5 min checks I gave up, figured I should let the regression pass and then work on it.
cx: Plans to retry once the nursery is ready after a move.

q: It’s currently 12:15 am. I’m writing this in tears as my husband tries for the umpeenth time tonight to put our son back to sleep.
cx: Mother of a nearly-17-month-old, a week after stopping breastfeeding cold turkey.

q: But I’m growing this resentment and anger during the bedtime process. He. Won’t. Stay. Asleep. I see other people say their kid sleeps all night or only wakes 1-2 times. He’s legit up like every 30minutes to an hour.
cx: What bedtime has become.

q: My husband says “he’s feeling your distraction, calm down” I CANT CALM DOWN IF ITS TAKING ME HOURS TO PUT HIM TO SLEEP!
cx: Husband's explanation for the wakings.

q: I need help bad. I don’t want to resent my baby, he’s trying to figure it out but I’m so tired of this.
cx: End of her post.

q: He sleeps perfectly fine at daycare. And it makes me so jealous that the teachers barely have to pat him to sleep.
cx: Daycare gets a 2.5-hour nap with little help.

q: Because he knows we will just give in so we can sleep. I need to do a major reconstruction with our approach. We need to sleep. I steered away from sleep training when he was younger but now we’re paying for it.
cx: Looking back on avoiding training as a baby.

q: Definitely not happening, if you don’t have any real advice then don’t comment.
cx: Reply to a commenter's suggestion she rejects.

q: We do 8:30 since my husband gets off at 6 and of course wants to spend time with him. I guess it’s not the season for that until we get this under control.
cx: Why bedtime is late.

q: He is a big help but he is also the one that goes to work during the daytime so I do try to do most of night time as I am a night shifter. But also yes I do feel gaslit sometimes, I wanna sleep!
cx: On the husband's role, after commenters question him.

q: I’ve started going to the park as soon as we get home or walk up and down the stairs 20 million times. He gets so tired now that he’s fussy by 6:45ish and goes down for the night with 1 wake up!!!
cx: Three days later, after a commenter's tip.

q: I have now weaned her off of nursing to sleep but she is still waking up every 2 hours. […] I have been trying to ferber method but she is absolutely hystetical and the check ins make it worse.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 9-month-old who wakes every two hours.

q: I have used the ferber method to sleep train children i have nannied but they were both  over than 1 and less than 2. Which i feel makes it easier and also it's a lot easier to listen to crying when it isnt your own baby
cx: A former nanny finds the method harder with her own baby.

q: My baby just turned one this week, and she sleeps in the living room. Is this bad parenting?
cx: Parent in a two-bedroom flat; baby sleeps 7–8 hours in a play yard, wakes every two hours in her cot.

q:
In her crib: wakes up every two hours. 

In her playpen: sleeps about 7-8hours.
cx: Her comparison of two sleep spots.

q: me and my partner have bought 4 different cribs to see if she’ll like a crib, and she just doesn’t.
cx: Asks for ideas to make a cot comfortable.

q: For a while she was sleeping from 9pm-7am with no wake ups. Now I can’t even get a couple hours in without her fussing. It’s been like this for over a month. […] I thought maybe we needed to adjust her nap schedule. I’ve tried several different schedules and none of them help.
cx: Parent of a 7-month-old posting at 2am after a month of broken nights.

q: My husband doesn’t hear her cry in his sleep so he’s no help at all. I just want a good nights sleep. I feel so exhausted.
cx: End of her 2am post.
